summary: Yasuhiro Okazaki works in Indology and philosophy. He earned a PhD from Hiroshima University, studying under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono, and held posts at Hiroshima Prefectural Chiyoda, Hiroshima Prefectural Kabe, and Takamiya high schools (until 2003).

Yasuhiro Sueki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a short-term study under George Baumann at Tübingen University Library (~1993–1994) and held posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2002–2020).
Yasuhiro Ueno specializes in Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University until 2003 and held a research post at Koyasan University.

Yasuke Ikari specializes in Indology. He studied under Masaaki Hattori (~1963–1969) and earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen (~1970–1978). He held posts at Kindai University, Kyoto University, and Harvard University.

Yasumasa Sekine specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1969–1973) and held academic posts at Japan Women's University, Gakushuin Women's College, University of Tsukuba (~1999–2014), and Kwansei Gakuin University (~2014).

Yasunori Ejima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and conducted overseas research at the University of Göttingen. He held posts at Rissho University Junior College, Nagaoka University of Technology, and the University of Tokyo.

Yasuo Deguchi is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1980–1989) and later held posts at the Nagoya Institute of Technology (~1998–2003) and Kyoto University (~2003–2013) as Associate Professor of Philosophy.

Yasuo Goto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has held teaching and research posts at Ryukoku University as a lecturer, Shuchiin University as a part-time lecturer, and Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College as a visiting researcher.
Yasuo Inamoto specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He held posts as a technical official at Nara National Museum (~1996–2004) and at Kyoto University (~2004–2016).

Yasuo Matsunami was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano (~1974–1979) and held posts as a researcher at Taisho University and as an advisor for the Sravakabhumi Study Group until 2010.
Yasuo Sano is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Study Group.

Yasuo Yuasa was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji and held positions at the University of Yamanashi, Osaka University, University of Tsukuba, and J. F. Oberlin University.

Yasuro Abe specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Wako University (~1972–1976) and served as a professor at Otemae University (~1983–1993), Osaka University (~1993–2003), and Nagoya University (~2003–2019).

Yasutaka Muroya specializes in Indology and philosophy. He has served as a project research associate at the University of Vienna and Leipzig University, and as a research associate at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (~2010).

Yasutoshi Murakami specializes in Buddhist studies. After studying at Tohoku University (~1960–1969), he held academic posts at Yamaguchi University (~1976–2000), Koyasan University (~2000–2012), and served as president of the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies (~2008–2013).
Yawen Yang is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fo Guang University from ~2006 to 2009, earning an MA under the supervision of Yongdong Shi.

Yi-hsun Huang specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia (~1994–2001) under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner and committee members Karen C. Lang, Gilbert Roy, David Germano, and Jinhua Chen.

Yifa is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She studied at National Taiwan University, under Hsing Yun, earned a master's at the University of Hawaii, and completed a PhD at Yale under Stanley Weinstein. She held posts at University of the West and Harvard.

Yigal Bronner specializes in Indology. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock (~1994–1999), later holding academic posts at the University of Chicago (~2002–2011) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~2011).

Yiliang Zhou was a scholar of history, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fu Jen Catholic University, Yenching University under Yinke Chen, and Harvard University, later serving as a professor at Peking University from ~1952 to 2001.
